proposed_features.description: Identifies the main subject of the text. Corporate entities and financial markets distinguish business/tech news from government/military actors in world news and athletes/teams in sports news.

Categorizes the fundamental type of event reported. This separates competitive outcomes (sports), market fluctuations (business), geopolitical conflicts/disasters (world), and technological developments (sci-tech).

Describes the primary numerical data used. Sports rely on scores and stats; business on financial metrics and prices; sci-tech on specs or adoption rates; world news often lacks specific quantitative focus or uses casualty counts.

Indicates the time frame of the impact. Sports are immediate; business is quarterly/annual; sci-tech is forward-looking or current adoption; world news is immediate to medium-term geopolitical shifts.

Captures the tone and vocabulary style. Sports use action verbs and slang; business uses formal financial jargon; sci-tech uses technical terminology; world news uses neutral, objective reporting language.
Identifies who is directly affected. Investors/employees (business), fans/athletes (sports), patients/consumers (sci-tech), citizens/international community (world).

Describes how the story is constructed. Sports often follow a play-by-play or summary structure; business follows a headline-then-detail financial report; sci-tech follows a problem-solution or feature-benefit structure; world news follows a who-what-where-when structure.

Highlights the primary cause-effect relationship. Sports: performance leads to win/loss; Business: market conditions lead to price change; Sci-tech: technology leads to efficiency/cost savings; World: political action leads to conflict/damage.
Indicates the geographic relevance. Sports are local/national; Business is global/national; Sci-tech is global/niche; World is regional/international.
Defines the purpose of the text. Sports: inform of result; Business: inform of financial status; Sci-tech: inform of capability/innovation; World: inform of event/impact.

Checks for direct speech. Sports often quote coaches/players; Business quotes executives; Sci-tech quotes engineers/analysts; World news quotes officials/witnesses. However, the *type* of quote is more discriminative, but presence is a basic feature.
Measures the level of abstraction. Sports are concrete (specific plays); Business is semi-abstract (market trends); Sci-tech is abstract (concepts, systems); World is concrete (specific incidents).
Assesses the perceived urgency. Sports: high (live/immediate); Business: medium (market open/close); Sci-tech: low (long-term); World: high (breaking news).
Describes the specificity of the entities mentioned. Sports: specific teams/players; Business: specific companies/tickers; Sci-tech: specific products/standards; World: specific countries/groups.
